title: Would I still recommend a Toyota Tundra after its engine recalls? - USA Today

 Are Tundra engine issues ruining the truck's reputation?
 Charles Singh USA TODAY Nov. 18, 2026, 3:43 p.m. ET Hear this story Toyota is recalling 62,000 non-hybrid Tundra trucks from various model years due to a faulty engine camshaft.
 Despite recent engine issues, a study by iSeeCars.com lists the Tundra as one of the longest-lasting vehicles.
 The Tundra's previous V8 engine was considered more reliable than the current 3.4-liter twin-turbo V6 base engine.
 Toyota is known for producing some of the most reliable trucks and SUVs on the market. Recently, the dependability of its full-size truck has been in question because of engine issues.
 Is the Toyota Tundra truly one of the most reliable pickup trucks in its segment, or should car buyers consider other options? Here's what you need to know about the Tundra's recent engine problems.
 Why the Toyota Tundra is being recalled
 The Japanese car brand is conducting a safety recall for non-hybrid Tundra models. Toyota says 62,000 vehicles are involved in the recall, including 2022, 2023, 2025 and 2026 model years.
 Tundras are being recalled because of a faulty engine camshaft. The camshaft could lead to a loss of power at high speeds.
 What to do if your Tundra is being recalled
 If your Tundra is recalled, you should book an appointment with a Toyota service department after receiving a recall notice. Notices are expected to be mailed out by mid-January 2027.
 The third-generation Toyota Tundra has been recalled four times for major engine issues related to the 3.4-liter twin-turbo V6 base engine.
 Is the Toyota Tundra reliable?
 Is Toyota's full-size pickup truck dependable or is it plagued with reliability issues following the removal of its V8 engine option?
 A study by automotive research site iSeeCars.com listed the Tundra as one of the longest-lasting vehicles. The study analyzed data for more than 395 million vehicles to see which models were the most likely to reach 250,000 miles.
 The worst problem category for the Tundra is engine problems, says user-submitted vehicle problem report site CarComplaints.com . Toyota's full-size pickup truck may be generally reliable, but recent model years have experienced serious recurring engine issues related to the latest engine.

Here's why Want to test a car for days before buying it? Here's one way you can What's new with the 2027 Toyota Tundra, and would I recommend it? New Tundras may be significantly more efficient following the removal of the standard V8 engine for the third generation, but the V8 was much more reliable than the current base engine. The Tundra isn't an unreliable pickup truck and retains its status as a long-lasting model.
 What full-size pickup truck should you get?
 There are plenty of popular Tundra alternatives for buyers to choose from in 2026. Two of the best-selling full-size trucks in America include the Ford F-150 and the Chevrolet Silverado 1500.
 Chevy's Silverado 1500 ($38,600) is the cheapest of the three models. The Tundra has the most powerful base engine (348 horsepower). Ford's F-150 is the most efficient of the three trucks as a base model.
 The Ford F-150 offers the overall best ownership experience in its segment because of its capability as a work truck and dependable engine options. If you're set on the Tundra nameplate, consider buying the hybrid over the gas model because of its reliability.
